nodes.name: Telegram Trigger
nodes.notes:
Trigger On is 'message' ONLY, not '*'. Every other update type produces executions that do nothing and make the list unreadable.

Additional Fields > Restrict to Chat IDs would filter here too, but it hardcodes your chat id into a file you are going to share. The guard node reads it from the environment instead. See BUILD-THE-BOT.md section 11.

nodes.name: Is this you?
nodes.notes: THE SECURITY MODEL. Runs before anything is downloaded. Returns an empty array for anyone who is not the owner, which stops the branch silently. Fails CLOSED if BRAIN_OWNER_ID is unset.

nodes.name: Voice note?
nodes.notes: A stranger gets silence. The owner never does - a text message gets told what to send instead.

nodes.name: Get the voice note
nodes.notes: Inbound is native - the token stays in the credential. Only the final sendVoice has to go out over raw HTTP, because this node has no sendVoice operation.

nodes.name: Save the ogg
nodes.notes:
{{ $execution.id }} in EVERY temp filename. A fixed name breaks the first time two voice notes arrive close together: the second execution overwrites the first one's audio mid-flight. It does not error - it sends the wrong answer.

If this fails with an access error, your n8n restricts file paths (N8N_RESTRICT_FILE_ACCESS_TO). Use a path under /home/node/ instead, here and in every ffmpeg command below.

nodes.name: ogg to mp3
nodes.notes: A Telegram voice note is ogg/opus. The transcription path was measured on MP3, not on ogg - the probe built an ogg clip and never sent it. Converting here puts this on the path that actually returned 200 in 1.7s, and ffmpeg is already in the container so it costs nothing.

nodes.name: Transcribe
nodes.notes:
The SAME OpenRouter key from Class 1. No new credential anywhere in this class.

A 404 here means the model slug was retired, not that the workflow is broken. google/gemini-2.0-flash-001 already went that way.

nodes.name: Ask the brain
nodes.notes:
CLASS 3, UNTOUCHED. This node runs inside the n8n container, where localhost:5678 is n8n itself - do not use a LAN address.

/webhook/ask, NOT /webhook-test/ask. The test URL only exists while the Class 3 editor is open and listening, so it works while you are watching and fails the moment you close the tab.

nodes.name: Send the text
nodes.notes: Sent BEFORE the voice note on purpose. Seeing the answer written down while you listen is better than either alone, and it is what you screenshot when something is wrong.

nodes.name: Speak it
nodes.notes:
TWO TRAPS, both 400s whose message is only in the response body:
  format mp3 + no stream  -> 'Audio output requires stream: true'
  format mp3 + stream     -> "does not support 'mp3' when stream=true"
  format pcm16 + stream   -> 200

Response Format must be 'text' or n8n throws on the SSE stream.

nodes.name: Reassemble the audio
nodes.notes:
Concatenate the base64 FIRST, decode ONCE. Decoding per frame and joining the bytes works by luck with base64 padding and breaks silently - the file is the right size and plays as static.

Reports audioFrames / pcmBytes / seconds. Zero frames means STOP; everything downstream will build a plausible file out of nothing.

nodes.name: To a voice note
nodes.notes: -f s16le -ar 24000 -ac 1 describe the RAW PCM and must come BEFORE -i. Raw PCM has no header saying what it is. Get any of the three wrong and ffmpeg still produces a file - it just sounds fast, slow, or like static.

nodes.name: sendVoice
nodes.notes:
No credential attached, deliberately. The token comes from $env.BRAIN_BOT_TOKEN.

404 here almost always means that variable is EMPTY in the container, not that the token is wrong - the URL became /bot/sendVoice. Check with: bash setup-telegram-private.sh --stack ~/brain --status

nodes.name: Clean up
nodes.notes: Every execution leaves four files in the container otherwise, and nothing removes them until the container is recreated.
